2026-07-28T22:xx follow-up (RTE two-foll.CRITICAL FINDING -- shadow rate limiter: services/worker/src/index.ts:377 `app.use('/api', rateLimiters.api, badgeRouter)` is a PREFIX mount on `/api` (not `/api/v1`), registered BEFORE `app.use('/api/v1', apiV1Router)` at index.ts:487. Per Express's own prefix-mount execution model (the same class of bug index.ts:368-376's comment documents fixing for `/api/v1/identity` specifically -- 'run their middleware for EVERY /api/* request... before the broad /api chokepoint can run'), `rateLimiters.api` (a 60 req/min-per-IP limiter, services/worker/src/utils/rateLimit.ts:190-193) executes for EVERY /api/v1/* request -- including /api/v1/verify/*/proof, /api/v1/anchor/*/lifecycle, /api/v1/usage -- before apiV1Router's own correctly-keyed 1000/min-per-API-key limiter (router.ts:199-203) ever runs. The SAME fix already applied for /api/v1/identity (mount it before the broad /api chokepoint) was NOT applied to the rest of apiV1Router. Confirmed live via worker stdout logs: `{"key":"<loadgen origin IP>","count":60,"maxRequests":60,"msg":"Rate limit exceeded"}` on both rigs, while the SAME request's own X-RateLimit-Limit header (from the later, correctly-keyed limiter that also ran and set its own header, unaware the earlier one already 429'd some requests) shows 1000 -- so the response header a client sees is NOT the limit actually enforced. This is a Constitution 1.10 compliance bug (documented 1,000/min for API-key holders, actual ~60/min per origin IP) independent of and pre-existing this soak; it is the reason the runbook's 28 RPS sustained / 83 RPS burst target is structurally unreachable from a small number of loadgen origin IPs, not a worker capacity limit.
